text: The Last Unicorn is a 1982 soundtrack album composed and arranged by Jimmy Webb and performed by America with the London Symphony Orchestra. The album features the film score for the 1982 film The Last Unicorn, which is based on the novel of the same name by Peter S. Beagle. The title track received airplay in Germany, where it remained in the Top 100 for seven weeks, peaking at number 38. The soundtrack was recorded at De Lane Lea Studios in Wembley, England in 1982 and was released in Germany in 1982 by Virgin Records; it has not been released in the United States and includes the film score's symphonic pieces. Studio singer Katie Irving provides the singing voice for Mia Farrow in the film, while Jeff Bridges performs his own singing. The album was released digitally in selected regions on 25 December 2025 and physically on 29 December 2025 by Polydor and Interscope Records. The title song is performed jointly by America and the London Symphony Orchestra and plays in the film's opening credits against scenes based on The Unicorn Tapestries; it serves as a leitmotif for other portions of the film score. In his review for AllMusic, James Christopher Monger awarded the album 4/5 stars, writing: "The score itself, an appropriately somber and sentimental blend of fairy tale motifs and dark, Wagnerian cues, reflects the story's achingly beautiful tale of a unicorn who attempts to overthrow a maniacal king determined to rid the world of the magical creatures, while the songs are far more creative, daring, and eloquent than all of the cookie-cutter balladry that would eventually replace their type in future animated films. Like Watership Down, The Hobbit, and even Robert Altman's live action, Harry Nilsson-scored Popeye, this hard to find soundtrack is a gem from another age." Kyle Anderson of Nerdist noted that Jimmy Webb and America were among the "many great people [who] were involved" with the 1982 film and that the album's "songs work pretty well." Singer Dan Avidan has stated on numerous occasions that the story was his favorite as a child. All tracks are written by Jimmy Webb.
